body:
When I was debugging the FFT I got to the individual samples by reverse engineering the spectrum array and recording their frequencies here: In this demo project when https://github.com/goatchurchprime/godot-demo-projects/blob/gtch/spectrum_analyser/audio/spectrum_analyzer/spectrum_plot.gd#L42

Getting the whole of the FFT array is a good idea, but the calculation it leaves stuff out like the imaginary components and it is non-overlapping.  (The [oversampling parameter in AudioEffectPitchShift](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_audioeffectpitchshift.html#class-audioeffectpitchshift-property-oversampling) is how many overlapping FFT windows are used in the recreation of the sound.)  

The deeper question is what do we do with the FFT values when we get them.  Usually it's to make nice visual effects related to the sound, often by passing it as a texture into a shader.  However the state of the art in terms of what can be done like this is [VRC AudioLink](https://github.com/llealloo/audiolink/tree/master/Docs) which delivers a structured texture into the GPU shader with lots of useful stuff, not just the FFT.  We should steal their ideas.

This, of course, would be a lot of feature creep and can and should be done in a GDExtension, and it is sensible to put a limit to how far this goes.

As such, this PR is a good place to leave it, as it does not extend the interface in terms of the values it can read, it simply accesses the same numbers with a more correct and efficient function.
